title: Evaluate Tier-1 Payment Gateways for European Card Expansion
author: marcus.vance
content:
Description:
FinFlow is expanding direct merchant acquiring into France and Germany scheduled for Q3 2024. This ticket documents the technical and commercial evaluation of three prospective payment gateway providers:

1. Provider X:
- Pros: Established French Cartes Bancaires (CB) and German Girocard clearing licenses; compatible with our legacy ISO 8583 settlement pipeline currently used by Tier-1 enterprise partner Apex Retail.
- Cons: Outdated SOAP/XML payload envelope; higher per-transaction markup (+28 bps); rigid batch settlement window.

2. Provider Y:
- Pros: Modern developer-first REST/JSON API, sub-120ms p99 latency, automated dispute webhooks.
- Cons: European banking license (BaFin) currently pending approval; cannot clear Cartes Bancaires or Girocard natively before Q4 2024 or Q1 2025. Co-badged EU transactions would fall back to costly international Visa/Mastercard interchange.

3. Provider Z:
- Pros: Low processing fees, competitive multi-currency FX rates.
- Cons: Lacks synchronous 3DS2 challenge callbacks; relies exclusively on asynchronous batched settlement webhooks (up to 6h delay) which breaks our ledger night-audit requirement.

Recommendation:
Select Provider X as the immediate path forward for the 2024 EU expansion despite architectural drawbacks, due to immediate local scheme compliance and zero disruption to the Apex Retail ISO 8583 dependency.

metadata.resolution: Provider X selected as temporary solution

title: Implement Legacy Payment Gateway Adapter for Provider X (Temporary Rail)
author: devon.chen
content:
Description:
Construct a translation adapter (`LegacyGatewayAdapter`) between the FinFlow payment orchestration engine and Provider X's legacy XML gateway endpoint.

Scope:
- Translate JSON authorization requests into Provider X's XML schema containing ISO 8583 fields (Field 3: Processing Code, Field 4: Transaction Amount, Field 48: Local Scheme Data for Cartes Bancaires).
- Maintain compatibility with Apex Retail's existing batch settlement pipeline.
- Add circuit breaker with 2500ms timeout for legacy socket connections.

Architectural Note:
This adapter is treated as a short-term workaround to expedite European market launch without rewriting our core settlement reconciliation service. It should be scheduled for deprecation once multi-rail unified processing is deployed.

title: Provider X Settlement Delay & Reconciliation Discrepancies
author: tariq.ahmed
content:
Description:
Finance operations reports recurring discrepancies in European merchant settlements. Provider X's service contract specifies T+1 settlement finality, but settlement batches over the past 6 weeks have consistently arrived at T+2 or T+3.

Impact:
- European merchant payouts delayed by up to 48 hours.
- Settlement-reconciliation service is forced to run compensating manual reconciliation jobs.
- Finance team has escalated penalty fees under Section 4.2 of the Provider X Master Services Agreement.

Root Cause Analysis:
Provider X's European clearing node in Frankfurt has experienced backlogs in processing local Girocard settlement batches. Provider X technical account team has failed to provide a permanent resolution.

title: Apex Retail Migration to REST API v2 Complete
author: alicia.m
content:
Description:
Apex Retail, FinFlow's highest-volume enterprise partner, has officially completed its multi-quarter migration from the legacy ISO 8583 protocol broker to FinFlow's modern REST API v2 (`/v2/payments/authorize` and `/v2/settlements/stream`).

Verification:
- 100% of Apex Retail live traffic (approx. 65k txns/day) is now routing through the v2 gateway.
- The legacy ISO 8583 socket server and batch files have been quiesced and have had zero inbound traffic for 7 consecutive days.
- Sign-off received from Apex Retail VP of Engineering.

Note:
The legacy ISO 8583 adapter infrastructure was originally kept active primarily to support Apex Retail's legacy protocol requirement. With this migration finished, this blocker has been eliminated.
